slots.hypothesis: The C axis: the correlation between minute return and minute volume, the axis built furthest from the other two in the library. Its only head is the triple-smoothed head8 (+0.53, sign +1). Raw day_corr carries two mechanical parts: the day's direction (on up days volume falls in up minutes) and volume-volatility comovement (MDH). Any alpha should be the alignment left after stripping both. The 12 seeds each use a different set of outer operators, and none is smoothing alone. They (1) bucket by the day's return day_sum(Ret), daily and then smoothed or the reverse, optionally adding the day_centroid(Ret) bucket from the A axis; (2) subtract or bucket out day_corr(abs_(Ret), Volume), as a linear-vs-bucket pair; (3) multiply the core by sign(day return) to test whether volume confirms the day's direction; (4) add a size-rank interaction (Llorente et al.), screens for late-volume and frozen-quote names, a 40-day lower-quartile tail mean, and daily bucketing by volume timing. head8 is in the reward controls, so pure re-smoothing earns nothing. Pure-smoothing measurement goes to R.

head1's mechanism (bare volume timing -0.09 -> bucketed within deciles of volatility timing +0.72 -> 20-day smoothing +1.55; the subtraction version only +0.83) is read as 'volume shape vs its volatility counterpart' (Admati-Pfleiderer). This slot moves the same treatment (20-day mean of a volume-shape statistic, z-scored inside the deciles of its volatility counterpart) to the non-timing dimensions: concentration (gini), persistence (AR1), spikiness (kurt / right-tail ES), volume-volatility comovement (MDH corr, top-10%-volume-minute impact). It also adds two other encodings of timing, plus controls for each: a linear subtraction version, an unconditioned sufficiency probe, and a version conditioned on day_centroid(Ret) instead. 15 seeds.

**Slot a, E on core `day_corr(Ret, Volume)` (the C axis).** I did not give the A axis another E slot: the library already holds 3-4 heads on it, and smoothing pushes it toward the known family. The core has 3 nodes, so the GP has room to change the smoothing. All 12 seeds contain the core verbatim. Their sets of outer operators all differ from each other and from the ones already seen in the snapshot ({}, {cross_mean}, {cross_mean, cross_sum}), and none hits a library structure ban. head8 sits in the reward controls and pure re-smoothing is likely blocked by the 0.7 library ban, so every seed instead strips or rewrites one of the two mechanical parts: the day's direction (via day_sum(Ret)) and the volume-volatility comovement (via day_corr(abs_(Ret), Volume)).

**Slot b, N: does head1's mechanism carry over beyond timing?** The 15 seeds take the same treatment (smoothed volume shape, z-scored within the deciles of its volatility counterpart) to concentration, persistence, spikiness and comovement. Each dimension has linear, unconditioned and alternative-conditioner controls. Round 1 already used an N slot, so the 'at least one N' rule is met either way.

**R: 16 variants across six heads.**
- head8: single 40/60-day windows, plus the A-axis conditioner moved onto it.
- head1: four conditioner swaps (smoothed version, gini, the known family, LogFloatCap as a placebo).
- head2: smoothed and 40% screens, LogFloatCap as y, and a liquidity placebo.
- head3: shell removed with a 10% band, plus band variable LogFloatCap or frozen quotes, to test price against size.
- head6: BoardCode in place of the buckets that currently follow the panel's column order.
- head4: daily bucketing, then smoothing.

I left bare LogFloatShares out of R because it ranks identically to an expression already scored (+0.48).

The notebook section records my current beliefs about this seed's alpha sources, numeric pre-registered predictions for every slot and every R variant, and a check of the round-1 predictions. Round 1 got the direction (late volume is bad) and the bare-core range right. It got wrong the claim that bucketing would not rescue the centroid: bucketing turned out to be the largest single gain.
